newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SRINATH TO SEE SURGEON IN SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRINATH TO SEE SURGEON IN SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Indian pace bowler Javagal Srinath, returning home from the West Indies with a sore shoulder, will see a surgeon in Johannesburg who had treated him during a tour of South Africa, cricket officials said on Sunday.

Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Jagmohan Dalmiya told reporters in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta that Srinath's request to see the same doctor who had treated him last month had been granted.
"We are making arrangements to fly him to Johannesburg to be examined by the surgeon of his choice," Dalmiya said.
"A decision on his replacement will be taken only after Srinath's condition was analysed by the surgeon," Dalmiya said.
Srinath, 27, complained of a sore shoulder during practice on the eve of India's opening tour game against Jamaica at Sabina Park in Kingston on Saturday.
Indian coach Madan Lal rejected suggestions that Srinath had arrived in the West Indies with the injury.
Srinath's shoulder first troubled him during the rigorous tour of South Africa where he carried the bulk of India's bowling attack along with medium pacer Venkatesh Prasad.

A cricket board official said Srinath had been advised to take three weeks' rest by the team's physiotherapist but it was unlikely that he would be pushed into service again during the nine-week tour of the West Indies.
But Dalmiya said if the South African surgeon's report was favourable Srinath might rejoin the team.

Dalmiya told reporters that surgery was not suggested by the doctor who examined him on the eve of the team's departure for the West Indies. The doctor had cleared him to bowl but refrain from throwing from the deep.
